messages:
harper_finance: Heads up — reseller flagged an unusual proration on their Azure Marketplace invoice. They say seats activated during DST switch were double-prorated and they were underbilled. Can we audit quickly?

sylvia_partners: Oh wow. do we have invoice id + subscription?

harper_finance: invoice INV-2026-11-05-res-312, sub: res-312, reseller: channel-aurora. They expected ~$1,320 owed but invoice is only $820. Looks like two proration passes occurred for mid-Oct activations.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-11-05-res-312 created for $820.00 (seats billed: 92 @ effective rates). Billing period: 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31.

tom_billing: can someone paste the meterline/events? need event timestamps and activation_ts.

harper_finance: meterlines (redacted):
2026-10-15T01:30:00-04:00,res-312,seats:+10,activation_ts:2026-10-15T01:30:00-04:00
2026-10-15T01:45:00-04:00,res-312,seats:+8,activation_ts:2026-10-15T01:45:00-04:00
2026-10-31T00:00:00Z,res-312,snapshot:92

harper_finance: note those activations happened during the US fall DST change (clocks moved back at 02:00). Partner says their connector sent both event_time and ingest_time as local timestamps.

tom_billing: if ingestion pipeline treated activation_ts as wall-clock without TZ normalization, we could've applied proration twice: once for local date segment and again after normalization. I'll check the proration routine logs.

ingest-bot: Created ticket TCK-6203: "Azure marketplace DST proration anomaly - res-312" assigned to eng-ops.

sylvia_partners: partner ops confirms they sent events with timezone offset -04:00 and did not include explicit UTC. They assumed our connector would infer DST. They provided raw webhook payloads.

tom_billing: found logs: proration service applied prorate_factor based on date boundaries in local time, then reconciliation job applied a second prorate when converting to UTC for storage because ingest_time normalization ran after proration. That double-step caused ~40% underbill on those new seats.

harper_finance: finance: what's the delta? reseller claims $500 owed. quick calc from logs: missing charges ~ $510.

harper_finance: propose: 1) issue retro invoice for missing $510, 2) notify AP and reseller, 3) patch proration pipeline to normalize timestamps before proration. Need approvals.

sylvia_partners: reseller prefers a single retro invoice vs a credit/collect mix. they'd rather be billed to catch up this period. Is finance comfortable with that?

harper_finance: finance lead approved issuing a corrective invoice for $510. AP will not hold payment. We still need eng to fix pipeline to avoid recurrence.

tom_billing: filed fix PR to normalize event timestamps to UTC prior to proration and added a regression test for DST transitions. Will heat-patch the proration microservice today.

ingest-bot: Note: Added alert to snapshot job to flag >5% variance between snapshoted seats and expected when events occur within DST boundary windows.

harper_finance: I'll send reseller a short explanation + corrective invoice and attach to TCK-6203. Also will log a vendor communication explaining expected event_time format (UTC recommended).

sylvia_partners: reseller ok with corrective invoice. They want the communication to mention we fixed the root cause.

billing-bot: Updated ticket TCK-6203 with action items and assigned to eng-ops. Corrective invoice INV-2026-11-05-CORR issued for $510.

harper_finance: closing loop — finance will monitor next billing cycle for same reseller and confirm no repeat. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
